cases.description: A schema with $id is schema-invalid, since its base URI would change what its relative $refs mean (§9.2, decision U14). check reports it once and checks the record for everything else.
YAML anchors and aliases in a schema file are schema-invalid, since schema files follow vmd's YAML rules (§9.2, decision U15). check reports it once and checks the record for everything else.
An x-vmd-list reached only through oneOf, off the spine, is schema-invalid (§9.3, decision U2). check reports it once and checks the record for everything else.
A keyed list with more than one key member is schema-invalid (§9.3, decision U8). check reports it once and checks the record for everything else.
unevaluatedItems beside x-vmd-list is schema-invalid, since it would fail valid data (§9.3, decision U16). check reports it once and checks the record for everything else.
$sections keyed by anything but ["@key"] is schema-invalid (§9.3, decision U17). check reports it once and checks the record for everything else.
x-vmd-ref on a string without format: uri-reference is schema-invalid, since it would do nothing (§9.3, decision U18). check reports it once and checks the record for everything else.
An x-vmd-summary that is not a boolean is schema-invalid (§9.3, decision U19). check reports it once and checks the record for everything else.
A record that two collections' globs match gets collection-conflict and is read unschematized; other records are unaffected (§9.1, decision U5).
A collection name must match [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*, so my/things is config-invalid (§9.1, decision U10).
A configuration member this version does not define is feature-unsupported, since a newer minor version may define it (§9.1, decision U21).
